q: According to Huygens' principle, every point on a wavefront acts as a source of
why: Huygens' principle states that each point on a wavefront emits secondary wavelets

q: Rays of light are always directed
why: Rays represent the direction of energy propagation, always normal to the wavefront

q: In Young's double slit experiment, the fringe width w is given by
why: Fringe width formula: w = lambda D / d, where D is slit-to-screen distance and d is slit separation

q: In Young's double slit experiment, a bright fringe is obtained when the path difference between the two waves is
why: Constructive interference (bright fringe) occurs when path difference = n lambda (n = 0,1,2,...)

q: In single slit diffraction of width a, the first minimum occurs at angle theta satisfying
why: First minimum of single-slit diffraction: a sin(theta) = lambda

q: If the wavelength of light used in Young's double slit experiment is increased, the fringe width
why: Since w = lambda D/d, increasing lambda increases fringe width w

q: Polarization of light demonstrates that light waves are
why: Only transverse waves can be polarized, confirming light is a transverse wave

q: Brewster's law relating the polarizing angle theta_B to refractive index n is
why: Brewster's law: tan(theta_B) = n, the refractive index of the medium

q: The resolving power of a telescope with aperture diameter D is
why: Since minimum resolvable angle theta = 1.22 lambda/D, resolving power = 1/theta is proportional to D

q: Diffraction effects become more prominent when the size of the obstacle or aperture is
o: much larger than the wavelength of light
comparable to the wavelength of light
why: Diffraction is significant when obstacle/slit size is comparable to the wavelength of the wave
